text:
Fort Wright Police to offer free scam and fraud awareness class on November 12
The Fort Wright Police Department will host a free scam and fraud awareness class on November 12. The event is open to all residents and aims to educate the community about protecting themselves from scams. The city continues to provide a range of services and community programs.
Residents are invited to attend a free scam and fraud awareness class hosted by the Fort Wright Police Department on November 12. The event will take place at the City of Fort Wright, located at 409 Kyles Lane in Fort Wright, Kentucky.
The class aims to educate community members about current scams and fraudulent activities, providing them with information to help protect themselves and their families. The police department encourages all interested individuals to participate in this initiative.
The Fort Wright Police Department maintains accreditation reflecting professional standards, according to the official website. The city operates as a municipal government and provides services including emergency response, infrastructure maintenance, and community parks. Fort Wright features an elected mayor and six council members, and supports community services such as passport assistance and transparent government operations, according to the official website.
Fort Wright is named after Civil War hero Maj. Gen. Horatio Gouverneur Wright and is known for its scenic hillside views of Cincinnati. The city includes parks such as Battery Hooper Park, which features a Civil War museum and recreational facilities, according to the official website.
The scam and fraud awareness class is part of the city's ongoing efforts to promote safety and community engagement. Additional information about city services and upcoming events can be found on the City of Fort Wright's official website.
